video.title: An Average Guy Built This in One Weekend. Here's How

summary: Chris Koerner interviews John Cheney, who vibe-coded an AI services business in a weekend, did $180k in six weeks and about $1M in six months, and now has 27 employees. The episode focuses on free customer acquisition: pitching local TV news with a human-interest angle (one segment brought $200-$300k of deals), press releases around partnerships (BYU athletics, Replit), daily authentic social posting, and posting as a whole person. Chris adds his Buc-ee's story, where one cold email to a Texas Monthly reporter led to $180k in sales and a business now making $1M+ net profit a year. Key takeaway: earned media and consistent posting are cheap, asymmetric bets, and fear of others' judgement is the real blocker.

tactics.name: Pitch local TV news with a packaged human-interest angle
steps: Get first customers and a result worth talking about first
Fill out the station's online news tip form or text a contact
State what you did, the angle, and why viewers get value
Avoid sounding like a free commercial
Expect same-day filming (25-30 min interview)
Follow up months later with new milestones bundled together
Build a personal PR network of reporters

quote.text: Here's the angle. Here's why other people would like to hear that.
quote.speaker: John Cheney

tactics.name: Leverage a partnership into a press release
steps: Land a credible partner (BYU athletics)
Ask a big company (Replit) to contribute (6 months free per athlete)
Get approved quotes from each party (can take weeks)
Distribute via PR Newswire (~$1,000)
Gain backlinks and pickup from Yahoo News, MSNBC, TechCrunch

tactics.name: Cold email reporters from bylines
steps: Find relevant articles and the writer's byline email
Send a one-line pitch of your story from Gmail
Email several reporters; a few respond
One article can cascade to others

quote.text: I bought one of everything, a buckies and I'm going to sell them on a website. Do you want to write about that?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: 30-day public gratitude posting challenge
steps: Post something you're grateful for every day for 30 days (John did 366)
Include at least one real failure you're grateful for
Optionally add a call to action asking followers what they're grateful for

quote.text: Every single day posts something you're grateful for. That's it.
quote.speaker: John Cheney

tactics.name: Jab, jab, jab, right hook content
steps: Post free value daily (reviews of AI tools, what you like/dislike)
Act like a reporter rather than selling
Occasionally make an ask

tactics.name: Post as a whole person on every platform
steps: Mix personal life (kayaking, family, piano) with work content
On LinkedIn, tie personal posts to professional lessons
Personal content raises DM response rates even with few followers

warnings.warning: Media won't give you a free commercial; pitches must be human interest or inspiring.

quote.text: they don't want to just do a free commercial for you. That's, that's the critical thing.
quote.speaker: John Cheney

warnings.warning: Don't spam reporters; only pitch with real news.

quote.text: Don't bother them. Don't spam them a bunch, right?
quote.speaker: John Cheney

warnings.warning: Telling stories about how awesome you are backfires; relate to the audience instead.

quote.text: A lot of people tell a story about themselves and they talk about how awesome they are.
quote.speaker: John Cheney

warnings.warning: Social media takes years of daily consistency; quitting after two months is too early.

quote.text: I was posting for two months and nobody followed me
quote.speaker: John Cheney

warnings.warning: Day trading consumed three months and lost $10k.
Press releases need approved quotes from partners and can take weeks.
UK: Playmakers teaches cold SMS/calls; in the UK cold SMS to individuals/sole traders breaches PECR and calls must be TPS/CTPS screened.
Transcript is Whisper tiny: names (John Cheney, company names) may be mis-heard.

lessons.lesson: People fear others' perception of failure, not failure itself.

quote.text: No one's afraid of failure. We're just afraid of what people will think if we fail.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Local news desks often have no backlog and want ready-made stories.
Do the reporter's job for them: package the story and the viewer benefit.

quote.text: Do their job for them.
quote.speaker: John Cheney

lessons.lesson: Sell the future desired state, not features.

quote.text: Telling that story of the future desired state is way better than saying, here's our benefits and features
quote.speaker: John Cheney

lessons.lesson: Platforms run on interest graphs; consistent topical posting finds the right audience.

quote.text: These social platforms are switching from a social graph to an interest graph.
quote.speaker: John Cheney

lessons.lesson: Earned media is an asymmetric bet: one email can be worth millions.

quote.text: The asymmetric bed of a lifetime, right? One email, millions of dollars, six years later.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Build in public; ideas are cheap, execution is what counts.

quote.text: The reality is execution is where is where, you know, the money lives.
quote.speaker: John Cheney

lessons.lesson: False constraints (build a business in one day) can force action.
Showing up in person can itself be the story angle.
Borrow credibility from bigger names via partnerships.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand with specific deal sizes but revenue figures unverified and Whisper tiny transcript garbles names.
